title: U.S. Sanctions Russia Again as Putin Warns of a Bigger War With NATO /Lt Col Daniel Davis
summary: A retired US officer argues sanctions on Russia are useless, Russia never meant to conquer Ukraine or attack Europe, NATO's war talk is the real danger, and the US cannot win its war with Iran.

assertions.quote: none of it has any effect at all

verdicts.note: Sanctions have cut Russia's oil revenue, technology access and growth, even though they have not stopped the war.

SIPRI finds Western sanctions forced Russia to re-route imports of dual-use components through non-sanctioning countries at higher prices, raising procurement costs, so they have had an effect though not a decisive one.
DDIS: Western sanctions exert intense pressure on Russia's economy, are a major factor in its reduced energy earnings, and have made military components more costly to obtain.
EFIS says sanctions 'clearly affect the Russian economy' and its defence industry, though loopholes remain.

US intelligence says Russia stays resilient to sanctions but at the cost of widening deficits, underinvestment, a risk of long-term stagnation and deeper dependence on China, so sanctions have had real costs.

assertions.quote: We have been advancing decade after decade towards Russia.
they're coming to get us we have to get ready for war by 2030 my god they're coming for us

verdicts.note: German, Danish and NATO assessments say Russia could rebuild forces for a war with NATO by about 2029-30; capability is not intent.

assertions.quote: There's no evidence at all that Russia is just chomping at the bit.

verdicts.note: Russia's intentions are not on the public record and its official denials cannot settle the question.
DDIS says Russia is preparing for a possible war against NATO but has not decided to wage one, and for now avoids triggering Article 5; it rearms to keep the option open.
EFIS states Russia has no intention of militarily attacking any NATO member in the coming year, but it limits this to the near term and ties it to continued deterrence.

assertions.quote: given the number of troops they sent in for the task, they clearly did not intend to militarily conquer Ukraine.

verdicts.note: RAND describes Russia's 'expansive goals at the outset', including capturing Kyiv and 'denazifying' the government, scaled back to annexing four provinces only after failure.

assertions.quote: they've gone up at least a half a million in their active force on the ground from what it was.

verdicts.note: Russia raised its authorised troop strength and expanded missile and drone production, though it has also lost many units in Ukraine.

assertions.quote: the offensive form of of missile warfare is way beyond the the uh the defensive warfare, way beyond the ability to knock these things down.

verdicts.note: Mass drone and missile salvos have saturated defences in Ukraine and the Gulf, but defences still intercept most incoming fire in many attacks.

assertions.quote: it's also infantile to sit there and say over and over with so much enthusiasm and and so self-confidence that that Russia is testing us
we can't bring them to heal. We have not been able to bring the Houthi people to heal.

verdicts.note: Years of Saudi, US and Israeli air campaigns degraded but did not stop Houthi missile and shipping attacks.

assertions.quote: They weren't pursuing one before according to your own administration. according to your intelligence.
No one's going to agree to anything with you because they're going to see your deal impervious.

verdicts.note: Plausible but unmeasured; Russia and Iran have kept negotiating with Washington despite its reversals.
